A1.justification: Both PDFs describe VisualPredicator. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–D support reliable comparison despite appendix renumbering and substantial reformatting.

before.justification: V1 reports original experiments across five simulated robotic domains, including comparative performance, an operator-learning ablation, learning trajectories, and planning statistics.

after.justification: V2 retains these original robotic experiments and appendix results, with limited updates to the plotted results.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 changes predicate-candidate retention. V1 resets the proposal pool each iteration and selects from new proposals plus previously selected predicates; v2 initializes a persistent pool and accumulates all proposals, allowing previously unselected candidates to be reconsidered. The overall learning architecture remains unchanged.

E1.justification: Both evaluate Cover, Blocks, Coffee, Cover Heavy, and Balance, retaining the same task requirements and generalization scenarios. Replacement scene illustrations do not establish additional evaluated environments or scenarios.

E2.justification: The evaluated comparators remain MAPLE, ViLa, Sym. pred., Ablate op., No invent, and Oracle. Their participation in Figure 4 and the corresponding appendix comparisons is unchanged.

E3.justification: Training-task counts, object-count splits, 50 test tasks per seed, planning budgets, metrics, and MAPLE's restriction to the training distribution are retained. V2's CPU/GPU and shared-controller descriptions disclose settings without establishing a protocol change.

E4.justification: The operator ablation, Coffee learning trajectory, learned-abstraction examples, and planning-efficiency analyses are retained. V1 Figure 5 becomes v2 Figure 6. The new predicate-interpretation example explains prompting without adding an evaluated ablation or robustness test.

E5.justification: Both report averaging over five random seeds and display error bars in Figure 4. No changed run count or uncertainty-estimation procedure is documented; changes to Oracle's plotted error-bar values accompany the result updates.

E6.justification: Figure 4 changes Oracle's Blocks solve rate from approximately 95% to 98% and planning-budget use from approximately 17% to 14%, with corresponding error-bar changes. The appendix numerical tables remain unchanged. Section 5.3 also newly reports that predicate search typically takes a few minutes on one CPU.

T1.justification: Appendix B.2 adds a complexity argument contrasting linear cluster-and-intersect processing with exponential dependence on predicate count for the additional search. Existing definitions and Equations (1)–(5) remain. Section 5.3 adds an argmin expression that conflicts with its retained highest-score wording.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central contributions: neuro-symbolic predicates, online abstraction learning, and advantages in sample efficiency, generalization, and interpretability across five simulated domains.

C2.justification: V2 Appendix B.5 adds an explanation of recovery through rejecting noisy predicates and proposing alternative descriptions. It expands potential remedies to probabilistic truth estimates and embedding comparisons, and predicts better perception on natural images. These are interpretations and prospective solutions, without new validating experiments.

D1.justification: V2 adds a concrete predicate-evaluation prompt, CPU/GPU allocation, shared hand-coded controller information, and search-time guidance. Appendix B.2 newly specifies using cluster-and-intersect inside predicate selection before applying the extended learner to selected predicates; this is newly documented implementation information, not evidence of changed execution.

R1.justification: The conclusion and bibliography add Huang et al. (2024), Liang et al. (2024), and Ma et al. (2023) to connect future skill acquisition with motion planning and reinforcement learning. The substantive related-work positioning in Section 7 remains unchanged.

P1.justification: V2 adds a predicate-interpretation subsection, expands search and limitations explanations, and makes localized wording and cross-reference edits. Conference headers are added, but the main narrative and section organization remain largely intact.

P2.justification: Figures 1 and 3 receive replacement scene renderings, and a new Figure 5 illustrates predicate interpretation. Appendix operator listings are extensively reformatted into wrapped boxes, resolving clipped lines and replacing side-by-side initial-operator layouts. Existing planning tables are relocated and jointly captioned as Table 1.

improvement.justification: V2 modestly improves reproducibility and readability through the worked prompt, implementation and complexity details, explicit candidate retention, and repaired appendix listings. The empirical foundation remains largely unchanged. These gains are qualified by the new argmin/highest-score inconsistency and unexplained Oracle plot updates alongside unchanged appendix table values.
